correctness.rationale: Exact level-population construction realizes each integer coefficient as a difference of positive layer counts, with equal component sizes from \(P(1)=0\). Fixed two-guru weighted plurality with independent competencies \(4/5\) and \(3/5\) has accuracy \(4/5\), \(7/10\), \(3/5\) according to the sign of the weight difference. Factorization of \(P_m\) proves exactly \(m\) positive intervals; a rational gap polynomial proves grid error at least \(1/10\). The star-minus-path difference \(t(1-t)\) proves strict six-voter interior improvement. For at most five voters, exhaustive guru-count cases give majority decisions fixed in the interior or one fair-tie crossing; neither permits an interior accuracy exceeding both endpoint accuracies. Exact-rational Python checks executed successfully: 4 polynomial families, 75 rational crosschecks, 1441 labeled small forests, 55 level signatures and 90 unique interior-breakpoint forests. Infinite assertions rest on proof, not this finite enumeration. No unproved generalization is claimed.

value.rationale: A motivated expressivity question about viscosity optimization in liquid delegation is resolved by exact realizability of arbitrary endpoint-vanishing integer depth polynomials. This entails an unbounded number of disconnected optimal parameter windows with only two gurus and equal component sizes, a constant accuracy failure for every predetermined finite grid, and an exact smallest witness at six voters. These limits are mathematically structural and actionable for choosing optimization strategies; no stronger claim about adaptive algorithms is made.
